translationRepairs: That sixth month an edict made Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting censor-in-chief, replaced Fumeng Lingcha as commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and recalled Lingcha to the capital.

That sixth month an edict made Xianzhi Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acting vice censor-in-chief, replaced Fumeng Lingcha as commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and recalled Lingcha to the capital.
鴻臚卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; 御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.

In the sixth month of that year an edict appointed Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Censor-in-Chief, replacing Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and summoning Lingcha to court.

In the sixth month of that year an edict appointed Xianzhi Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, replacing Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and summoning Lingcha to court.
鴻臚卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; 御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.
When Xianzhi's army reached Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no envoy from the capital to welcome them and cursed him: "Korean cur who eats dog guts!
When Xianzhi's army reached Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one at all to welcome them and cursed him: "Korean cur who eats dog guts!
都不使人 means sent no one at all; 都 is not the capital here.
When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one from the capital to welcome or comfort them, and cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one at all to welcome or comfort them, and cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
都不使人 means sent no one at all; 都 is not the capital here.
In the eighth year he came to court, was granted special advancement, and was made full grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, with one son given a fifth-rank post.
In the eighth year he came to court, was granted special advancement, and was made full grand general of the Left Jinwu (Imperial Insignia) Guard, with one son given a fifth-rank post.
金吾 is Jinwu, the imperial insignia (mace) guard; 吾 is not "crow".
In the eighth year he came to court, was given the special advancement rank, and concurrently made full Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, with one son granted a fifth-rank office.

In the eighth year he came to court, was given the special advancement rank, and concurrently made full Grand General of the Left Jinwu (Imperial Insignia) Guard, with one son granted a fifth-rank office.
金吾 is Jinwu, the imperial insignia (mace) guard; 吾 is not "crow".
Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he took more than ten large blocks of kingfisher jade, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades beyond count.

Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he took more than ten large blocks of sese gems (a blue precious stone), five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades beyond count.
瑟瑟 is a blue gemstone (sese), not kingfisher jade.

Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he obtained more than ten large stones of kingfisher feathers, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in proportion.

Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he obtained more than ten large stones of sese gems (a blue precious stone), five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in proportion.
瑟瑟 is a blue gemstone (sese), not kingfisher feathers.

At first Sheji had regarded Xianzhi as timid and slow, fearing he could not support himself; now that he had won merit, his household wealth ran to tens of thousands and he could give generously—when anyone asked something of him, he never refused to speak.

At first Sheji had regarded Xianzhi as timid and slow, fearing he could not support himself; now that he had won merit, his household wealth ran to tens of thousands and he could give generously—when anyone asked something of him, he never failed to grant it.
言無不應 means he granted every request.

That year he came to court, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Tripod, and soon after removed as Administrator of Wuwei and Military Commissioner of Hexi, replacing An Sishun.

That year he came to court, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Tripod, and soon after appointed Administrator of Wuwei and Military Commissioner of Hexi, replacing An Sishun.
除 here means appointed to office.
From then on Changqing attended Xianzhi's comings and goings, never leaving his gate from dawn till dusk. After some ten days Xianzhi gave in and made him a retainer.
From then on Changqing attended Xianzhi's comings and goings, never leaving his gate from dawn till dusk. After several dozen days Xianzhi gave in and made him a retainer.
凡數十日 is several tens of days.
Soon afterward he was promoted to Master of Spreading Morality and given sole charge of the granaries, garrison farms, armor and weapons, supply accounts, and military colonies of the Four Garrisons.

Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Master for Court Discussion (chaosan dafu) and given sole charge of the granaries, garrison farms, armor and weapons, supply accounts, and military colonies of the Four Garrisons.
朝散大夫 is the prestige title chaosan dafu, not "spreading morality".

Shortly thereafter he was further promoted to Master of Spreading Morality, placed exclusively in charge of the four garrisons' granaries, garrison agriculture, armor and weapons, supply accounting, and military colony affairs.

Shortly thereafter he was further promoted to Grand Master for Court Discussion (chaosan dafu), placed exclusively in charge of the four garrisons' granaries, garrison agriculture, armor and weapons, supply accounting, and military colony affairs.
朝散大夫 is the prestige title chaosan dafu, not "spreading morality".

While serving as rear-affairs commissioner, Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dequan already held the rank of colonel; Dequan's mother lived in the residence, and Xianzhi treated the household as his own kin, entrusting all domestic affairs to Changqing's oversight until his authority commanded the whole army.

While serving as rear-affairs commissioner, Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dequan already held the rank of colonel; Dequan's mother lived in the residence, and Xianzhi treated Dequan like a brother and entrusted all household affairs to him, so that his prestige swayed the whole army.
視之如兄弟，家事皆令知之 refers to Zheng Dequan, not Feng Changqing.

While managing rear affairs, Xianzhi's wet-nurse's son Zheng Dequan was already a colonel; Dequan's mother lived within the residence, and Xianzhi treated her son like a brother—all household matters were entrusted to Changqing's knowledge, and his prestige moved the entire army.

While managing rear affairs, Xianzhi's wet-nurse's son Zheng Dequan was already a colonel; Dequan's mother lived within the residence, and Xianzhi treated her son like a brother—all household matters were entrusted to his (Dequan's) management, and his prestige moved the entire army.
家事皆令知之 refers to Zheng Dequan, not Feng Changqing.

In the eleventh year, after Zhengjian's death, Changqing was made deputy grand protector of Anxi, acting censor-in-chief, and with imperial commission was appointed deputy commissioner for the military administration, frontier strategy, supply, and military colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, with full authority over the command.

In the eleventh year, after Zhengjian's death, Changqing was made deputy grand protector of Anxi, acting vice censor-in-chief, and with imperial commission was appointed deputy commissioner for the military administration, frontier strategy, supply, and military colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, with full authority over the command.
御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.

In the eleventh year, Zhengjian died, and Changqing was appointed Deputy Grand Protector of Anxi, acting Censor-in-Chief, bearing the imperial credential as Deputy Commissioner for the Military Commission, Frontier Strategy, Supply, and Military Colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, managing commissioner affairs.

In the eleventh year, Zhengjian died, and Changqing was appointed Deputy Grand Protector of Anxi, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, bearing the imperial credential as Deputy Commissioner for the Military Commission, Frontier Strategy, Supply, and Military Colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, managing commissioner affairs.
御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.

In the thirteenth year he came to court and was named acting chief censor; one of his sons received a fifth-rank appointment, he was granted a first-rank residence, and both his deceased parents were posthumously ennobled.

In the thirteenth year he came to court and was named acting chief censor; one of his sons received a fifth-rank appointment, he was granted a residence, and both his deceased parents were posthumously ennobled.
賜第一區 means granted one residence (一區), not a first-rank one.

In the thirteenth year he entered court; he was acting Chief Censor, and a fifth-rank post was granted to one of his sons, a premier residence was bestowed, and his deceased parents were both posthumously ennobled.

In the thirteenth year he entered court; he was acting Chief Censor, and a fifth-rank post was granted to one of his sons, a residence was bestowed, and his deceased parents were both posthumously ennobled.
賜第一區 means granted one residence (一區).

Before long, Cheng Qianli, grand protector of Beiting, was recalled to the capital as right general of the Gold Crow Guard, and Changqing was temporarily entrusted with the Beiting protectorate, bearing imperial commission as commissioner of Yixi and related territories.

Before long, Cheng Qianli, grand protector of Beiting, was recalled to the capital as grand general of the Right Jinwu Guard, and Changqing was temporarily entrusted with the Beiting protectorate, bearing imperial commission as commissioner of Yixi and related territories.
右金吾大將軍 is grand general of the Right Jinwu (Imperial Insignia) Guard.

Soon afterward Grand Protector of Beiting Cheng Qianli entered the capital as Right General of the Gold Crow Guard; Changqing was temporarily appointed to administer Beiting Grand Protectorate, bearing the credential as Commissioner of Yixi and related posts.

Soon afterward Grand Protector of Beiting Cheng Qianli entered the capital as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard; Changqing was temporarily appointed to administer Beiting Grand Protectorate, bearing the credential as Commissioner of Yixi and related posts.
右金吾大將軍 is grand general of the Right Jinwu (Imperial Insignia) Guard.
Changqing sent his best horsemen to meet the Tuqishi vanguard in battle and killed several hundred of the enemy.
Changqing sent his best horsemen to meet the Zhejie (Chakar) warriors vanguard in battle and killed several dozen to a hundred of the enemy.
柘羯 are Zhejie (Sogdian chakar) troops, not the Tuqishi. 數十百人 is several tens to a hundred.
"I have read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen how Lang Zhi lamented that he had not yet found the place to die—I have found mine at last."
"I have read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen how Lang Shen lamented that he had not yet found the place to die—I have found mine at last."
狼瞫 is read Láng Shěn.
Changqing sent crack cavalry to meet the Tuqishi in battle and killed several tens or hundreds of the enemy.
Changqing sent crack cavalry to meet the Zhejie (Chakar) warriors in battle and killed several tens or hundreds of the enemy.
柘羯 are Zhejie (Sogdian chakar) troops, not the Tuqishi.
"Your servant has read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen that Lang Zhi said he had not yet found the place to die—your servant has found it now."
"Your servant has read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen that Lang Shen said he had not yet found the place to die—your servant has found it now."
狼瞫 is read Láng Shěn.
"Leading market folk from the Zhou and Nan wards against the shock cavalry of Fanyang, we still piled the slain so thick upon the road that blood soaked the fields."
"Leading the market folk of Zhounan (Luoyang) against the shock cavalry of Yuyang, we still piled the slain so thick upon the road that blood soaked the fields."
周南 is the Luoyang region, not two wards; 漁陽 is Yuyang.
"Leading the masses of Zhou and Nan markets against the Fanyang shock cavalry, we still blocked the road with slain enemies until blood covered the fields."
"Leading the market masses of Zhounan (Luoyang) against the Yuyang shock cavalry, we still blocked the road with slain enemies until blood covered the fields."
周南 is the Luoyang region; 漁陽 is Yuyang.
Xianzhi returned to the hall, and Lingcheng gathered more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying, "The Grand Marshal has an edict as well."
Xianzhi returned to the hall, and Lingcheng gathered more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying, "Your Excellency has an edict as well."
大夫 addresses Gao Xianzhi (censor-in-chief, yushi dafu), not a grand marshal.
Xianzhi returned to the hall; Lingcheng summoned more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying: "The Grand Marshal also has an edict of grace."
Xianzhi returned to the hall; Lingcheng summoned more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying: "Your Excellency (the censor-in-chief) also has an edict of grace."
大夫 addresses Gao Xianzhi as yushi dafu.
The Han family was rich. Ge Shuhan was bold and chivalrous, delighted in honoring his promises, and prone to gambling and drinking.
Han's family was rich. He was bold and chivalrous, delighted in honoring his promises, and prone to gambling and drinking.
翰 is Geshu Han; his name is not split Ge Shuhan, and "Han family" misreads 翰家.
The Han family was wealthy in property. He was free-spirited and chivalrous, fond of keeping his word, and given to gambling and wine.
Han's family was wealthy in property. He was free-spirited and chivalrous, fond of keeping his word, and given to gambling and wine.
翰家 is Geshu Han's household.
He first served under the military commissioner Wang Yun. When Yun attacked Xincheng, he put Han in charge of the campaign, and the entire army was awestruck.
He first served under the military commissioner Wang Chui. When Chui attacked Xincheng, he put Han in charge of the campaign, and the entire army was awestruck.
王倕 is read Wáng Chuí. 倕 is read Chuí.
At first he served Military Commissioner Wang Yun. When Yun attacked Xincheng, he had Han oversee operations; the whole army was without exception awed and intimidated.
At first he served Military Commissioner Wang Chui. When Chui attacked Xincheng, he had Han oversee operations; the whole army was without exception awed and intimidated.
王倕 is read Wáng Chuí. 倕 is read Chuí.

An imperial order summoned Han to court. The emperor found him pleasing in conversation and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting censor-in-chief, with Han replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with full charge of the circuit.

An imperial order summoned Han to court. The emperor found him pleasing in conversation and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting vice censor-in-chief, with Han replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with full charge of the circuit.
御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.

An edict summoned Han to court. The emperor was pleased in conversation with him and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting censor-in-chief, replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with charge of circuit administration.

An edict summoned Han to court. The emperor was pleased in conversation with him and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting vice censor-in-chief, replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with charge of circuit administration.
御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.
In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shufang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were placed under Han's overall command to attack Shibao Fort.
In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shuofang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were placed under Han's overall command to attack Shibao Fort.

When An Lushan rose in rebellion, the emperor—after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and executed—recalled Han and appointed him grand marshal of the heir apparent's vanguard army. Tian Liangqiu served as acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning served as staff generals. With troops from Hexi, Longyou, and Shufang, foreign auxiliaries, and Gao Xianzhi's old soldiers—two hundred thousand in all—he was to hold the rebels at Tong Pass.

When An Lushan rose in rebellion, the emperor—after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and executed—recalled Han and appointed him grand marshal of the heir apparent's vanguard army. Tian Liangqiu served as acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning served as staff generals. With troops from Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang, foreign auxiliaries, and Gao Xianzhi's old soldiers—two hundred thousand in all—he was to hold the rebels at Tong Pass.
In the fifteenth year he was further appointed Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and given the rank of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
In the fifteenth year he was further appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the rank of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shangshu sheng), not of the Secretariat.
In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shufang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were entrusted to Han to command the assault on Shibao Fort.
In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shuofang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were entrusted to Han to command the assault on Shibao Fort.

When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and killed, the emperor summoned Han, appointed him Grand Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Vanguard Army, made Tian Liangqiu acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff, and Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning staff generals, with Hexi, Longyou, Shufang troops and foreign soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops totaling two hundred thousand, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.

When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and killed, the emperor summoned Han, appointed him Grand Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Vanguard Army, made Tian Liangqiu acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff, and Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning staff generals, with Hexi, Longyou, Shuofang troops and foreign soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops totaling two hundred thousand, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
In the fifteenth year he was further made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
In the fifteenth year he was further made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shangshu sheng), not of the Secretariat.
In the eleventh year he was further given the Palace-and-Procession status of Third Rank.
In the eleventh year he was further given the Palace-and-Procession status equal to the Three Excellencies.
儀同三司 means ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, not third rank.

Your Majesty is a ruler who restores order amid chaos. The empire is not yet settled. Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian holds Henan, and Lu Kui holds Nanyang. Keep me alive, and with a single letter I can win them over—the realm will be pacified in no time."

Your Majesty is a ruler who restores order amid chaos. The empire is not yet settled. Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Zhen holds Henan, and Lu Jiong holds Nanyang. Keep me alive, and with a single letter I can win them over—the realm will be pacified in no time."
來填 is a variant writing of the general 來瑱, Lai Zhen. 魯炅 is read Lǔ Jiǒng.

Ge Shuhan, broken by illness at home, was suddenly given sole command. Two hundred thousand men held the gate against the rebels, yet he no longer handled military affairs himself and delegated them to men ill suited for the role.

Geshu Han, broken by illness at home, was suddenly given sole command. Two hundred thousand men held the gate against the rebels, yet he no longer handled military affairs himself and delegated them to men ill suited for the role.
The surname is Geshu (哥舒) and the given name Han (翰).

Your Majesty is a lord who settles chaos. The realm is not yet pacified. Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian at Henan, and Lu Kui at Nanyang. Keep me here, and with a single letter I can summon them—they will submit in no time and the realm will be pacified."

Your Majesty is a lord who settles chaos. The realm is not yet pacified. Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Zhen at Henan, and Lu Jiong at Nanyang. Keep me here, and with a single letter I can summon them—they will submit in no time and the realm will be pacified."
來填 is a variant writing of the general 來瑱, Lai Zhen. 魯炅 is read Lǔ Jiǒng.

Ge Shuhan, incapacitated at home, was raised to sole command of the army. Two hundred thousand men held the pass against the rebels, yet he did not personally attend to military affairs and entrusted them to men unsuited to the task.

Geshu Han, incapacitated at home, was raised to sole command of the army. Two hundred thousand men held the pass against the rebels, yet he did not personally attend to military affairs and entrusted them to men unsuited to the task.
The surname is Geshu (哥舒) and the given name Han (翰).

Consider Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's oversight of the frontier tribes—yet also his meddling in military affairs—and one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone, nor condemn them without reservation.

Consider Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's supervision of the army—both hamstrung military command—and one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone, nor condemn them without reservation.
護戎 is supervising the army; both men interfered with command (掣肘於軍政).

Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's protection of the frontier tribes, yet also his interference in military affairs, one cannot wholly blame the three commanders alone, nor should one condemn them without qualification.

Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's supervision of the army, which likewise hampered military affairs, one cannot wholly blame the three commanders alone, nor should one condemn them without qualification.
護戎 is supervising the army; both men interfered with command (掣肘於軍政).
